commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: doctor

1	"""The NightJar web app: one server-rendered page plus a small JSON API.
2	
3	Run with:  uv run uvicorn nightjar.web:create_app --factory --reload
4	"""
5	
6	import os
7	from collections.abc import Callable
8	from datetime import UTC, datetime, time
9	from pathlib import Path
10	
11	from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request, UploadFile
12	from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse
13	from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
14	from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
15	from pydantic import BaseModel
16	
17	from nightjar.coach import Coach, ask_coach, get_coach
18	from nightjar.coach.service import DEFAULT_TRACE_PATH
19	from nightjar.diary import Diary, local_input_to_aware, parse_csv
20	from nightjar.models import Night, User
21	from nightjar.nudge import next_nudge
22	from nightjar.sleep_window import usual_bedtime
23	
24	HERE = Path(__file__).parent
25	Clock = Callable[[], datetime]
26	
27	
28	def system_clock() -> datetime:
29	    return datetime.now(UTC)
30	
31	
32	class CoachQuestion(BaseModel):
33	    question: str
34	
35	
36	def create_app(
37	    diary: Diary | None = None,
38	    coach: Coach | None = None,
39	    clock: Clock = system_clock,
40	    trace_path: Path = DEFAULT_TRACE_PATH,
41	) -> FastAPI:
42	    diary = diary or Diary(os.environ.get("NIGHTJAR_DB", "nightjar.db"))
43	    coach = coach or get_coach()
44	    templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=HERE / "templates")
45	    app = FastAPI(title="NightJar")
46	    app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=HERE / "static"), name="static")
47	
48	    def render(request: Request, status_code: int = 200, **extra) -> HTMLResponse:
49	        user, nights = diary.user(), diary.nights()
50	        context = {
51	            "user": user,
52	            "nights": nights,
53	            "usual_bedtime": usual_bedtime(nights),
54	            "nudge": next_nudge(user, nights, clock()),
55	            "imported": request.query_params.get("imported"),
56	            **extra,
57	        }
58	        return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", context, status_code=status_code)
59	
60	    @app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
61	    def home(request: Request):
62	        return render(request)
63	
64	    @app.post("/nights")
65	    def add_night(
66	        request: Request,
67	        bedtime: str = Form(...),
68	        wake_time: str = Form(...),
69	        timezone: str = Form(...),
70	        notes: str = Form(""),
71	    ):
72	        try:
73	            diary.add_night(
74	                Night(
75	                    bedtime=local_input_to_aware(bedtime, timezone),
76	                    wake_time=local_input_to_aware(wake_time, timezone),
77	                    timezone=timezone,
78	                    notes=notes.strip(),
79	                )
80	            )
81	        except ValueError as error:
82	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=str(error))
83	        return RedirectResponse("/", status_code=303)
84	
85	    @app.post("/import")
86	    async def import_csv(request: Request, file: UploadFile):
87	        try:
88	            nights = parse_csv((await file.read()).decode("utf-8-sig"))
89	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
90	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=f"Import failed. {error}")
91	        count = diary.add_nights(nights)
92	        return RedirectResponse(f"/?imported={count}", status_code=303)
93	
94	    @app.post("/settings")
95	    def save_settings(
96	        request: Request,
97	        timezone: str = Form(...),
98	        quiet_start: str = Form(""),
99	        quiet_end: str = Form(""),
100	    ):
101	        try:
102	            diary.save_user(
103	                User(
104	                    name=diary.user().name,
105	                    timezone=timezone.strip(),
106	                    quiet_start=time.fromisoformat(quiet_start) if quiet_start else None,
107	                    quiet_end=time.fromisoformat(quiet_end) if quiet_end else None,
108	                )
109	            )
110	        except ValueError as error:
111	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=str(error))
112	        return RedirectResponse("/", status_code=303)
113	
114	    @app.post("/coach", response_class=HTMLResponse)
115	    def coach_page(request: Request, question: str = Form(...)):
116	        answer = ask_coach(coach, diary.nights(), question, trace_path)
117	        return render(request, question=question, answer=answer)
118	
119	    @app.get("/api/nudge")
120	    def api_nudge():
121	        nudge = next_nudge(diary.user(), diary.nights(), clock())
122	        if nudge is None:
123	            return {"nudge": None, "reason": "Log at least 7 nights to get a nudge."}
124	        return {
125	            "nudge": {
126	                "at": nudge.at.isoformat(),
127	                "local_time": f"{nudge.at:%H:%M}",
128	                "silent": nudge.silent,
129	                "text": nudge.text,
130	            }
131	        }
132	
133	    @app.post("/api/coach")
134	    def api_coach(body: CoachQuestion):
135	        answer = ask_coach(coach, diary.nights(), body.question, trace_path)
136	        return {"answer": answer.text, "used_fallback": answer.used_fallback}
137	
138	    return app
139

"""Sleep diary storage (SQLite) and CSV import.

Datetimes are stored in UTC (ISO 8601) so they sort correctly; each night keeps
the IANA time zone the user was in, so local times can always be rebuilt.
"""

import csv
import io
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, time
from pathlib import Path

from nightjar.models import Night, User, zone

DEFAULT_USER = User(
    name="Sam", timezone="America/Toronto", quiet_start=time(23, 0), quiet_end=time(7, 0)
)
CSV_COLUMNS = {"bedtime", "wake_time", "timezone", "notes"}

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nights (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    bedtime_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
    wake_time_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
    timezone TEXT NOT NULL,
    notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_settings (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    timezone TEXT NOT NULL,
    quiet_start TEXT,
    quiet_end TEXT
);
"""


class Diary:
    """All reads and writes for one user's diary."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.path = str(path)
        with self._connect() as db:
            db.executescript(SCHEMA)

    @contextmanager
    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        db = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
        try:
            with db:  # commits on success, rolls back on error
                yield db
        finally:
            db.close()

    def add_night(self, night: Night) -> None:
        with self._connect() as db:
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO nights (bedtime_utc, wake_time_utc, timezone, notes)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    _to_utc_text(night.bedtime),
                    _to_utc_text(night.wake_time),
                    night.timezone,
                    night.notes,
                ),
            )

    def add_nights(self, nights: list[Night]) -> int:
        for night in nights:
            self.add_night(night)
        return len(nights)

    def nights(self) -> list[Night]:
        """All nights, newest first."""
        with self._connect() as db:
            rows = db.execute(
                "SELECT id, bedtime_utc, wake_time_utc, timezone, notes"
                " FROM nights ORDER BY bedtime_utc DESC"
            ).fetchall()
        return [
            Night(
                id=row[0],
                bedtime=datetime.fromisoformat(row[1]),
                wake_time=datetime.fromisoformat(row[2]),
                timezone=row[3],
                notes=row[4],
            )
            for row in rows
        ]

    def user(self) -> User:
        with self._connect() as db:
            row = db.execute(
                "SELECT name, timezone, quiet_start, quiet_end FROM user_settings"
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return DEFAULT_USER
        return User(
            name=row[0],
            timezone=row[1],
            quiet_start=_parse_time(row[2]),
            quiet_end=_parse_time(row[3]),
        )

    def save_user(self, user: User) -> None:
        zone(user.timezone)  # validate before saving
        with self._connect() as db:
            db.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO user_settings VALUES (1, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    user.name,
                    user.timezone,
                    _format_time(user.quiet_start),
                    _format_time(user.quiet_end),
                ),
            )

"""Journal search: unit tests for matching and API/page tests."""

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.search import matches
from nightjar.web import create_app


@pytest.fixture
def client(tmp_path):
    app = create_app(
        diary=Diary(tmp_path / "test.db"),
        coach=MockCoach(),
        clock=lambda: datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Toronto")),
        trace_path=tmp_path / "coach.jsonl",
    )
    return TestClient(app)


def add_note(client, day, notes):
    return client.post(
        "/nights",
        data={
            "bedtime": day + "T23:00",
            "wake_time": day + "T23:30",
            "timezone": "America/Toronto",
            "notes": notes,
        },
    )


def test_matches_exact_case_insensitive_and_typos():
    assert matches("Had Coffee late", "coffee")
    assert matches("Had coffee late", "cofee")
    assert matches("Had coffee late", "coffe late")
    assert not matches("Had coffee late", "tea")
    assert not matches("Had coffee late", "   ")


def test_short_words_need_exact_match():
    assert not matches("red light", "bed")


def test_search_api_tolerates_typos(client):
    add_note(client, "2026-03-10", "Had coffee late, restless")
    add_note(client, "2026-03-11", "Read a book, slept well")
    body = client.get("/api/search", params={"q": "cofee"}).json()
    assert body["query"] == "cofee"
    assert [n["notes"] for n in body["nights"]] == ["Had coffee late, restless"]
    assert client.get("/api/search", params={"q": "zzzz"}).json()["nights"] == []
    assert client.get("/api/search").json()["nights"] == []


def test_search_page_shows_search_text_escaped_and_results(client):
    add_note(client, "2026-03-10", "Had coffee late")
    page = client.get("/search", params={"q": "coffee"})
    assert "Results for: coffee" in page.text
    assert "Had coffee late" in page.text
    evil = client.get("/search", params={"q": "<script>x</script>"})
    assert "<script>x</script>" not in evil.text
    assert "<script>" in evil.text

Journal search is in and `make test` and `make lint` pass, but I couldn't run `make e2e`. The sandbox wouldn't approve it, so the Playwright test hasn't run against the changed page.

- **Test results:** `make test` gave `70 passed, 1 deselected`, and `make lint` gave `All checks passed!` and `33 files already formatted`.
- **API:** `GET /api/search?q=...` returns `{"query": ..., "nights": [...]}`. Each night has `id`, `night_of`, `bedtime`, `wake_time`, `timezone` and `notes`. Bedtime and wake time are in that night's local zone. An empty or missing `q` returns no nights.
- **Home page:** there is a "Search journal" box that submits to `GET /search?q=...`, which renders the home page with the results. It shows "Results for: <your text>" above the matching nights, or "No matching nights." The search text is HTML-escaped, and a test covers that.
- **Typo tolerance:** I used the standard library's `difflib`, so there is no new dependency and I didn't run `uv add`.
  - Matching is case-insensitive, and every word in the query has to match some word in the note.
  - Query words of four or more letters can differ slightly from the note word, so "cofee" finds "coffee".
  - Shorter words must match exactly, so "bed" doesn't match "red".
  - The 0.8 similarity cutoff is a guess. You can adjust it in `src/nightjar/search.py`.
- **Tests and docs:** the new tests are in `tests/test_search.py`, and I added a line for them to `docs/traceability.md`.

Please run `make e2e` yourself before merging. Nothing is committed.
